Migrating AGDI to a new machine

This guide migrates a AGDI Gateway from one machine to another without redoing onboarding.

The migration is simple conceptually:

  • Copy the state directory ($AGDI_STATE_DIR, default: ~/.agdi/) — this includes config, auth, sessions, and channel state.
  • Copy your workspace (~/.agdi/workspace/ by default) — this includes your agent files (memory, prompts, etc.).

But there are common footguns around profiles, permissions, and partial copies.

Before you start (what you are migrating)

1) Identify your state directory

Most installs use the default:

  • State dir: ~/.agdi/

But it may be different if you use:

  • --profile <name> (often becomes ~/.agdi-<profile>/)
  • AGDI_STATE_DIR=/some/path

If you’re not sure, run on the old machine:

agdi status

Look for mentions of AGDI_STATE_DIR / profile in the output. If you run multiple gateways, repeat for each profile.

2) Identify your workspace

Common defaults:

  • ~/.agdi/workspace/ (recommended workspace)
  • a custom folder you created

Your workspace is where files like MEMORY.md, USER.md, and memory/*.md live.

3) Understand what you will preserve

If you copy both the state dir and workspace, you keep:

  • Gateway configuration (agdi.json)
  • Auth profiles / API keys / OAuth tokens
  • Session history + agent state
  • Channel state (e.g. WhatsApp login/session)
  • Your workspace files (memory, skills notes, etc.)

If you copy only the workspace (e.g., via Git), you do not preserve:

  • sessions
  • credentials
  • channel logins

Those live under $AGDI_STATE_DIR.

Migration steps (recommended)

Step 0 — Make a backup (old machine)

On the old machine, stop the gateway first so files aren’t changing mid-copy:

agdi gateway stop

(Optional but recommended) archive the state dir and workspace:

# Adjust paths if you use a profile or custom locations
cd ~
tar -czf agdi-state.tgz .agdi

tar -czf agdi-workspace.tgz .agdi/workspace

If you have multiple profiles/state dirs (e.g. ~/.agdi-main, ~/.agdi-work), archive each.

Step 1 — Install AGDI on the new machine

On the new machine, install the CLI (and Node if needed):

  • See: Install

At this stage, it’s OK if onboarding creates a fresh ~/.agdi/ — you will overwrite it in the next step.

Step 2 — Copy the state dir + workspace to the new machine

Copy both:

  • $AGDI_STATE_DIR (default ~/.agdi/)
  • your workspace (default ~/.agdi/workspace/)

Common approaches:

  • scp the tarballs and extract
  • rsync -a over SSH
  • external drive

After copying, ensure:

  • Hidden directories were included (e.g. .agdi/)
  • File ownership is correct for the user running the gateway

Step 3 — Run Doctor (migrations + service repair)

On the new machine:

agdi doctor

Doctor is the “safe boring” command. It repairs services, applies config migrations, and warns about mismatches.

Then:

agdi gateway restart
agdi status

Common footguns (and how to avoid them)

Footgun: profile / state-dir mismatch

If you ran the old gateway with a profile (or AGDI_STATE_DIR), and the new gateway uses a different one, you’ll see symptoms like:

  • config changes not taking effect
  • channels missing / logged out
  • empty session history

Fix: run the gateway/service using the same profile/state dir you migrated, then rerun:

agdi doctor

Footgun: copying only agdi.json

agdi.json is not enough. Many providers store state under:

  • $AGDI_STATE_DIR/credentials/
  • $AGDI_STATE_DIR/agents/<agentId>/...

Always migrate the entire $AGDI_STATE_DIR folder.

Footgun: permissions / ownership

If you copied as root or changed users, the gateway may fail to read credentials/sessions.

Fix: ensure the state dir + workspace are owned by the user running the gateway.

Footgun: migrating between remote/local modes

  • If your UI (WebUI/TUI) points at a remote gateway, the remote host owns the session store + workspace.
  • Migrating your laptop won’t move the remote gateway’s state.

If you’re in remote mode, migrate the gateway host.

Footgun: secrets in backups

$AGDI_STATE_DIR contains secrets (API keys, OAuth tokens, WhatsApp creds). Treat backups like production secrets:

  • store encrypted
  • avoid sharing over insecure channels
  • rotate keys if you suspect exposure

Verification checklist

On the new machine, confirm:

  • agdi status shows the gateway running
  • Your channels are still connected (e.g. WhatsApp doesn’t require re-pair)
  • The dashboard opens and shows existing sessions
  • Your workspace files (memory, configs) are present
